commands.author: pgondhi987

target.title: Harden jq safe-bin semantics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators can explicitly configure exec safe bins for narrow stdin-oriented tools. `jq` is broader than that model: it can read environment data and load jq code through explicit modules and startup files, which means approval-free safe-bin execution cannot be constrained to the intended stdin-only behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes `jq` fail closed in the safe-bin semantic gate, matching the existing treatment for other tools whose semantics cannot be validated to stdin-only. Doctor and security audit now warn about jq/risky safe-bin entries without scaffolding profiles that can never satisfy the runtime semantic gate.

Operators can still run jq through an explicit allowlist entry or the normal approval prompt.

## User Impact

`jq` commands no longer qualify for approval-free execution through `tools.exec.safeBins`, even for simple field filters. Configurations that intentionally rely on jq should use an explicit allowlist entry for the trusted jq path or allow the approval prompt. Other safe-bin tools such as `head`, `tail`, `tr`, and `wc` are unchanged.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-bin-semantics.test.ts src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-safe-bins.test.ts src/infra/exec-safe-bin-runtime-policy.test.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/exec-safe-bins.test.ts src/security/audit-exec-safe-bins.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-config.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals.test.ts`
  - Result: 3 Vitest shards passed, 227 tests passed.
  - Local fallback used because Testbox/Crabbox was unavailable in this environment: installed `crabbox` is `0.20.0`, while the Testbox wrapper requires a newer binary; direct AWS fallback also lacked broker configuration.
- `review-pr` review-only artifacts validated for head `0fc1e1178a8e100e0d72b1cd4d76d6ea1717b67e`; findings: 0.
- `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` passed for head `0fc1e1178a8e100e0d72b1cd4d76d6ea1717b67e`; no accepted/actionable findings.


## Current-head behavior proof

Head: `0fc1e1178a8e100e0d72b1cd4d76d6ea1717b67e`

- `node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-pr102032-jq-safe-bin-proof.mjs`
- Denied `jq 'include "envdump"; envdump'` as a safe-bin match: `allowlistSatisfied: false`, `segmentSatisfiedBy: [null]`.
- Denied `jq '($ENV).OPENAI_API_KEY'` as a safe-bin match: `allowlistSatisfied: false`, `segmentSatisfiedBy: [null]`.
- Preserved the supported trusted jq path: `jq .foo` with explicit `{ pattern: "/usr/bin/jq" }` allowlist returned `allowlistSatisfied: true`, `segmentSatisfiedBy: ["allowlist"]`.
- Preserved benign stdin-only safe-bin behavior: `head -n 1` with `tools.exec.safeBins: ["head"]` returned `allowlistSatisfied: true`, `segmentSatisfiedBy: ["safeBins"]`.

Compatibility note: existing configs that put jq in global or agent-scoped `tools.exec.safeBins` intentionally stop getting approval-free jq execution. Operators should use explicit allowlist entries for trusted jq paths or keep jq behind the approval prompt. Auth, sandbox mode, provider/plugin/channel behavior, and storage formats are unchanged.


## Real CLI security-audit proof

Head: `0fc1e1178a8e100e0d72b1cd4d76d6ea1717b67e`

- `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-pr102032-security-audit-config/openclaw.json OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr102032-security-audit-config/state pnpm openclaw security audit --json`
- Isolated config contained `tools.exec.safeBins: ["jq"]` and `tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.jq: {}`.
- Audit result included `tools.exec.safe_bins_broad_behavior` at `warn` severity with remediation: `Remove these binaries from safeBins and prefer explicit allowlist entries or approval-gated execution.`
- Local policy proof also showed jq module/env probes are not safe-bin satisfied before execution, while explicit `/usr/bin/jq` allowlist and `head` safe-bin controls still pass.
